ambiguities.statement: ContractRef membership inconsistently represents owners, consumers, mandatory reconciliation docs, and historical lineage.
Approve And Build sounds executable although the same map prohibits runtime launch and build artifacts.
Live Plans stabilization and the distinction between index-only refresh and governance sealing lack one explicit actor/state oracle.
Instant Grep runtime-field promotion and browser signal_confidence schema ownership lack a named owner and promotion/registration oracle.
Phase D uses an inconsistent Contracts_V0 path form, relies on truly necessary, and provides no promotion oracle from blocked provider scope to ready scope.
The threshold that promotes Contracts_V0 from MUST VERIFY to MUST RECONCILE is qualitative.
Worktree visibility has several allowed surfaces but no trigger or surface precedence, while handoff identity currentness is unstated.
Debug references an unidentified earlier minimum checklist, and terminal canonical behavior is jointly owned without an exact per-field partition.

builder_discretion.statement: Choose among workspace, file header, Source Control strip, editor status, or breadcrumb for conditional worktree visibility, without repeating it on every row/tab.
Additive command/GitHub deepening and minimal Contracts V0 examples are permitted when judged necessary, subject to retirement and phase-order constraints.
Chat and audit consumers may decide whether to raise clarification, but the canonical owner map controls the final target.
Builders determine when live Plans are stable enough for an allowed index refresh, while broader governance and node/build outputs remain prohibited.
Builders determine when remote identity, freshness, health, or write-availability fields have crossed from prose into persisted/event canon, triggering Contracts V0 reconciliation.
Provider taxonomy, routing internals, settings layout, and ordering UX remain intentionally outside ready-now implementation scope.

candidate_findings.finding: ContractRef-driven discovery may include historical lineage, omit mandatory terminal/Debug docs, and miss the instantiated PRD runtime JSON while retaining only its schema.
Approve And Build may be implemented as launch authority despite the explicit non-executable compile boundary.
Index-only and governance-seal phase language may permit premature refresh of Spec Lock, shards, evidence, graph, or auto_decisions.
Instant Grep runtime fields and signal_confidence lack explicit schema/registration ownership and promotion rules.
Approval mapping lacks failure, ambiguity, replay, and duplicate-resolution behavior before runtime mutation.
Browser cleanup relies on unstable raw line-number cues in other documents.
Source Control handoff preserves repo/worktree identifiers but lacks a currentness and failure contract.
Ready-versus-blocked provider scope and discretionary phase-D additions lack deterministic advancement criteria.

claims.claim: PRD Builder owns intake through Approved PRD Pack and the explicit Planning Wizard handoff; Planning Wizard owns PlanningRun, topic work, conversion/audit, ApprovedPlanPack, compile readiness, GUI states, and Approve And Build.

Testing and downstream PlanCompile, Executor, WorkNodeRecord, activation, receipt, and Goal Runtime contracts have named owners and strict JSON/schema scenarios, but this compile enables no runtime/build artifacts; legacy wizard names remain compatibility-only and governance outputs require their designated later phases.

Goal_Runtime_System owns durable native Goal Mode behavior, scheduling, child goals, write authority, verification, completion receipts, and evidence; chat and GUI docs own visible controls and model placement, while contract, persistence, permission, artifact, model/account/provider, ledger, and PlanUnit owners supply registered data without creating nodes.

Instant Grep authority is split among Tools for query/fallback semantics and index-used events, storage for formats/publication/dirty-layer recovery, Final GUI for indexing visibility, and GitHub Integration for remote verification and no-silent-local-fallback behavior; ambiguous consumers defer to the canonical owner map.

Section 15 is browser behavior SSOT, rewrite-tie-in-memo owns rewrite constraints, GUI/file/command docs consume placement and actions, signal_confidence has four locked values, and stale browser engines, hosts, permission matrices, and historical newfeatures ownership are retired.

The index is not slash-command, permission, GUI-presentation, or persisted-payload SSOT; reconciliation is ordered across command, tool/permission, GUI, and persistence owners, with ready-now web scope separated from blocked provider-runtime decisions.

Artifact, persistence, shared event, tool policy, HITL UX, and permission authority are split; request_id must resolve to canonical blocked_sequence before mutation, and new approvals use scoped blocked_sequence, approval_scope_key, and ordered allowed_action_ids without generic widening.
Terminal behavior, persistence, GUI, consumers, commands, events, and routing have named owners; omitting UI Command Catalog, Contracts V0, or Wiring Matrix makes a terminal packet non-buildable.

File-manager/editor reconciliation fixes owner boundaries for remote retry, LSP, OpenFile/shared buffers, persistence, GUI, command wiring, browser cleanup, remote contract promotion, and repo/worktree handoff; repo_id and worktree_id must survive Source Control handoff while FileManager does not own worktree lifecycle.

Debug Mode authority is split across chat UI, runtime/permission/storage, browser automation, artifacts/contracts/prompts/tools, and consumers; two named document trios are mandatory packet-integrity gates.

cross_window_seams.statement: Preceding context establishes compile/testing/executor/runtime/model/GUI/worktree/receipt/ledger ownership and the non-executable governance boundary that must align with the core PRD and Goal maps.
Following context reinforces Section 15, Final GUI, FileManager, storage, retired Chain Wizard, Planning Ledger, and Plan Document roles consumed by the core ownership splits.
The capsule names adjacent windows WIN-00-plans-index-0002 and WIN-00-plans-index-0004; neither was inspected.

invalid_reason: Substantive reviewer agent identities were reused across successive window/role assignments, violating the Fresh Agent Isolation Protocol.

negative_space_observations.statement: The compile descriptions prohibit runtime launch, runtime artifacts, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, manifests, GoalRuns, implementation/build tasks, dispatch, and Orchestrator builds.
Legacy wizard names, historical browser material, stale engines/hosts/permission models, allowed_actions, and generic approval widening cannot become peer canon.
The index and consumer docs must not re-own schemas, permission rules, presentation payloads, freshness/fallback behavior, persistence, or worktree lifecycle.
No retry, cancel, resume, timeout, duplicate-invocation, or idempotency behavior is stated for the two planning approval entrypoints.
No missing, stale, ambiguous, duplicate, or replay behavior is stated for request_id-to-blocked_sequence resolution.
No unknown-value, versioning, migration, or downgrade behavior is stated for signal_confidence, browser capability fields, or promoted remote identity/health fields.
Official-source capability research has no stated freshness threshold, refresh trigger, or unavailable-source behavior in this map.
repo_id and worktree_id preservation lacks stated behavior for missing, stale, or conflicted identities.
